paragraphs.sourceText: Being a good parent is what every parent would like to be. But defining what it means to be a good parent is undoubtedly very 1 , particularly since children respond differently to the same style of parenting. A calm, rule-following child might respond better to a different sort of parenting than, 2 , a younger one.
paragraphs.translationZh: 做一个好父母，是每个父母都想成为的。但定义成为一个好父母意味着什么无疑是非常棘手的，特别是因为孩子们对相同的养育方式有不同的反应。例如，一个冷静、遵守规则的孩子可能比年幼的孩子对不同类型的养育方式有更好的反应。

paragraphs.sourceText: 3 , there’s another sort of parent that’s easier to 4 : a patient parent. Children of every age benefit from patient parenting. Still, 5 every parent would like to be patient, this is no easy 6 . Sometimes, parents get exhausted and are unable to maintain a 7 style with their kids. I understand this.
paragraphs.translationZh: 幸运的是，还有另一种更容易描述的父母：耐心的父母。每个年龄段的孩子都会从耐心的养育中受益。尽管如此，虽然每个家长都希望保持耐心，但这并不是一件容易的事。有时，父母会精疲力竭，无法对孩子保持宽容的态度。我明白这一点。

paragraphs.sourceText: You’re only human, and sometimes your kids can 8 you just a little too far. And then the 9 happens: You lose your patience and either scream at your kids or say something that was too 10 and does nobody any good. You wish that you could 11 the clock and start over. We’ve all been there.
paragraphs.translationZh: 你只是凡人，有时你的孩子可能会把你逼得太过分。然后不可避免的事情就会发生：你失去了耐心，要么对你的孩子尖叫，要么说一些过于严厉、对任何人都没有好处的话。你希望时光倒流，重新开始。我们都去过那里。

paragraphs.sourceText: 12 , even though it’s common, it’s vital to keep in mind that in a single moment of fatigue, you can say something to your child that you may 13 for a long time. This may not only do damage to your relationship with your child but also 14 your child’s self-esteem.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，尽管这种情况很常见，但重要的是要记住，在疲劳的一瞬间，你可能会对你的孩子说一些你可能会后悔很长时间的话。这不仅会损害您与孩子的关系，还会影响孩子的自尊。

paragraphs.sourceText: If you consistently lose your 15 with your kids, then you are modeling a lack of emotional control for your kids. We are all becoming increasingly aware of the 16 of modeling patience for the younger generation. This is a skill that will help them all throughout life. In fact, the ability to maintain emotional control when 17 by stress is one of the most significant of all life’s skills.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果你总是对孩子失去冷静，那么你就是在给孩子树立缺乏情绪控制的榜样。我们都越来越意识到为年轻一代树立耐心的重要性。这是一项对他们一生都有帮助的技能。事实上，面对压力时保持情绪控制的能力是所有生活技能中最重要的技能之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: Certainly, it’s 18 to maintain patience at all times with your kids. A more practical goal is to try to be as calm as you can when faced with 19 situations involving your children. I can promise you this: As a result of working toward this goal, you and your children will benefit and 20 from stressful moments feeling better physically and emotionally.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，对孩子始终保持耐心是很困难的。一个更实际的目标是，当面对涉及孩子的困难情况时，尽量保持冷静。我可以向您保证：通过努力实现这一目标，您和您的孩子将从压力时刻中受益，并在身体和情感上感觉更好。

paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读下面四篇课文。选择 A、B、C 或 D 来回答每篇课文后的问题。在答题卡上标记您的答案。 （40分）

paragraphs.sourceText: Rats and other animals need to be highly attuned to social signals from others so they can identify friends to cooperate with and enemies to avoid. To find out if this extends to non-living beings, Laleh Quinn at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues tested whether rats can detect social signals from robotic rats.
paragraphs.translationZh: 老鼠和其他动物需要高度适应来自他人的社交信号，这样它们才能识别出要合作的朋友和要避开的敌人。为了查明这种现象是否适用于非生物体，加州大学圣地亚哥分校的拉勒·奎恩 (Laleh Quinn) 和她的同事测试了老鼠是否能够检测到来自机器老鼠的社交信号。

paragraphs.sourceText: They housed eight adult rats with two types of robotic rat — one social and one asocial — for four days. The robot rats were quite minimalist, resembling a chunkier version of a computer mouse with wheels to move around and colourful markings.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他们将八只成年老鼠与两种类型的机器老鼠（一种是社交型的，一种是非社交型的）一起饲养了四天。机器鼠非常简约，类似于一个厚重版本的电脑鼠标，带有可以移动的轮子和彩色标记。

paragraphs.sourceText: During the experiment, the social robot rat followed the living rats around, played with the same toys, and opened cage doors to let trapped rats escape. Meanwhile, the asocial robot simply moved forwards and backwards and side to side.
paragraphs.translationZh: 实验过程中，社交机器鼠跟随活体老鼠四处走动，玩同样的玩具，并打开笼门让被困的老鼠逃脱。与此同时，非社交机器人只是简单地前后左右移动。

paragraphs.sourceText: Next, the researchers trapped the robots in cages and gave the rats the opportunity to release them by pressing a lever. Across 18 trials each, the living rats were 52 percent more likely on average to set the social robot free than the asocial one. This suggests that the rats perceived the social robot as a genuine social being. They may have bonded more with the social robot because it displayed behaviours like communal exploring and playing. This could lead to the rats better remembering having freed it earlier, and wanting the robot to return the favour when they get trapped, says Quinn.
paragraphs.translationZh: 接下来，研究人员将机器人困在笼子里，让老鼠有机会通过按下杠杆来释放它们。在每项 18 项试验中，活体老鼠释放社交机器人的可能性平均比非社交老鼠高出 52%。这表明老鼠将社交机器人视为真正的社交存在。他们可能与社交机器人有更多的联系，因为它表现出公共探索和玩耍等行为。奎因说，这可能会让老鼠更好地记住早些时候释放了它，并希望机器人在它们被困时回报它。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Rats have been shown to engage in multiple forms of reciprocal help and cooperation, including what is referred to as direct reciprocity — where a rat will help another rat that has previously helped them,” says Quinn.
paragraphs.translationZh: 奎因说：“研究表明，老鼠会参与多种形式的互惠帮助和合作，包括所谓的直接互惠——一只老鼠会帮助另一只曾经帮助过它们的老鼠。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The readiness of the rats to befriend the social robot was surprising given its minimal design. The robot was the same size as a regular rat but resembled a simple plastic box on wheels. “We’d assumed we’d have to give it a moving head and tail, facial features, and put a scent on it to make it smell like a real rat, but that wasn’t necessary,” says Janet Wiles at the University of Queensland in Australia, who helped with the research.
paragraphs.translationZh: 考虑到社交机器人的简约设计，老鼠愿意与社交机器人成为朋友的意愿令人惊讶。该机器人与普通老鼠大小相同，但类似于一个带轮子的简单塑料盒子。帮助这项研究的澳大利亚昆士兰大学的珍妮特·威尔斯（Janet Wiles）说：“我们原以为必须给它一个会动的头和尾、面部特征，并在上面喷上气味，让它闻起来像一只真正的老鼠，但那是没有必要的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The finding shows how sensitive rats are to social cues, even when they come from basic robots. Similarly, children tend to treat robots as if they are fellow beings, even when they display only simple social signals. “We humans seem to be fascinated by robots, and it turns out other animals are too,” says Wiles.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这一发现表明，老鼠对社交线索非常敏感，即使这些线索来自基本的机器人。同样，孩子们倾向于将机器人视为同胞，即使它们只显示简单的社交信号。 “我们人类似乎对机器人着迷，事实证明其他动物也是如此，”怀尔斯说。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is true that CEO pay has gone up — top ones may make 300 times the pay of typical workers on average, and since the mid-1970s, CEO pay for large publicly traded American corporations has, by varying estimates, gone up by about 500%. The typical CEO of a top American corporation now makes about $18.9 million a year.
paragraphs.translationZh: 确实，首席执行官的薪酬已经上涨——高层管理人员的平均薪酬可能是普通员工的 300 倍，而且自 20 世纪 70 年代中期以来，美国大型上市公司的首席执行官薪酬（根据不同的估计）上涨了约 500%。美国顶级公司首席执行官的典型年薪约为 1890 万美元。

paragraphs.sourceText: The best model for understanding the growth of CEO pay is that of limited CEO talent in a world where business opportunities for the top firms are growing rapidly. The efforts of America’s highest-earning 1% have been one of the more dynamic elements of the global economy. It’s not popular to say, but one reason their pay has gone up so much is that CEOs really have upped their game relative to many other workers in the U.S. economy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 理解首席执行官薪酬增长的最佳模型是在顶级公司的商业机会快速增长的世界中有限的首席执行官人才。美国收入最高的 1% 人群的努力已成为全球经济中最具活力的因素之一。这种说法并不流行，但他们的薪酬上涨如此之多的原因之一是，相对于美国经济中的许多其他工人，首席执行官确实提高了自己的水平。

paragraphs.sourceText: Today’s CEO, at least for major American firms, must have many more skills than simply being able to “run the company.” CEOs must have a good sense of financial markets and maybe even how the company should trade in them. They also need better public relations skills than their predecessors, as the costs of even a minor slipup can be significant. Then there’s the fact that large American companies are much more globalized than ever before, with supply chains spread across a larger number of countries. To lead in that system requires knowledge that is fairly mind-boggling. Plus, virtually all major American companies are becoming tech companies, often with their own research and development. And beyond this, major CEOs still have to do all the day-to-day work they have always done.
paragraphs.translationZh: 今天的首席执行官，至少对于美国大公司来说，必须拥有更多的技能，而不仅仅是能够“经营公司”。首席执行官必须对金融市场有良好的了解，甚至可能对公司应该如何在金融市场进行交易有很好的了解。他们还需要比前任更好的公共关系技能，因为即使是很小的失误也会造成巨大的损失。事实上，美国大公司比以往任何时候都更加全球化，供应链遍布更多国家。要领导这个系统，需要相当令人难以置信的知识。此外，几乎所有美国大公司都在成为科技公司，而且通常拥有自己的研发能力。除此之外，主要首席执行官仍然必须完成他们一直在做的所有日常工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: The common idea that high CEO pay is mainly about ripping people off doesn’t explain history very well. By most measures, corporate governance has become a lot tighter and more rigorous since the 1970s. Yet it is principally during this period of stronger governance that CEO pay has been high and rising. That suggests it is in the broader corporate interest to recruit top candidates for increasingly tough jobs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 人们普遍认为首席执行官的高薪主要是为了敲诈别人，但这并不能很好地解释历史。从大多数标准来看，自 20 世纪 70 年代以来，公司治理变得更加严格和严格。然而，主要是在治理更加强有力的时期，首席执行官的薪酬一直很高，而且还在不断上涨。这表明，招聘顶尖候选人来应对日益艰巨的工作符合更广泛的企业利益。

paragraphs.sourceText: Furthermore, the highest CEO salaries are paid to outside candidates, not to the cozy insider picks, another sign that high CEO pay is not some kind of depredation at the expense of the rest of the company. And the stock market reacts positively when companies tie CEO pay to, say, stock prices, a sign that those practices build up corporate value not just for the CEO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 此外，最高的首席执行官薪酬是支付给外部候选人的，而不是舒适的内部人选，这另一个迹象表明，高额首席执行官薪酬并不是以牺牲公司其他部门为代价的某种掠夺。当公司将首席执行官的薪酬与股票价格挂钩时，股市会做出积极反应，这表明这些做法不仅为首席执行官创造了公司价值。

paragraphs.sourceText: Madrid was hailed as a public health guiding light last November when it rolled out ambitious restrictions on the most polluting cars. Seven months and one election day later, a new conservative city council suspended enforcement of the clean air zone, a first step toward its possible termination. Mayor José Luis Martínez-Almeida made opposition to the zone a centrepiece of his election campaign, despite its success in improving air quality. A judge has now overruled the city’s decision to stop levying fines, ordering them restored. But with legal battles ahead, the zone’s future looks uncertain at best.
paragraphs.translationZh: 去年11月，马德里对污染最严重的汽车实施了雄心勃勃的限制，被誉为公共卫生的指路明灯。七个月和一个选举日后，新的保守派市议会暂停了清洁空气区的执法，这是其可能终止的第一步。尽管该区域在改善空气质量方面取得了成功，但市长何塞·路易斯·马丁内斯-阿尔梅达仍将反对该区域作为其竞选活动的核心内容。一名法官现已驳回该市停止征收罚款的决定，并下令恢复罚款。但随着未来的法律斗争，该地区的未来充其量也充满不确定性。

paragraphs.sourceText: Madrid’s back and forth on clean air is a pointed reminder of the limits to the patchwork, city-by-city approach that characterises efforts on air pollution across Europe, Britain very much included.
paragraphs.translationZh: 马德里在清洁空气问题上的来回反复提醒人们，欧洲（包括英国）在空气污染问题上采取的拼凑、逐个城市的做法是有局限性的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Among other weaknesses, the measures cities must employ when left to tackle dirty air on their own are politically controversial, and therefore vulnerable. That’s because they inevitably put the costs of cleaning the air on to individual drivers — who must pay fees or buy better vehicles — rather than on to the car manufacturers whose cheating is the real cause of our toxic pollution.
paragraphs.translationZh: 除其他弱点外，城市在自行解决空气污染问题时必须采取的措施在政治上存在争议，因此很脆弱。这是因为他们不可避免地将清洁空气的成本转嫁给了个别司机——他们必须支付费用或购买更好的车辆——而不是转嫁给汽车制造商，而汽车制造商的作弊行为是我们有毒污染的真正原因。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s not hard to imagine a similar reversal happening in London. The new ultra-low emission zone (Ulez) is likely to be a big issue in next year’s mayoral election. And if Sadiq Khan wins and extends it to the North and South Circular roads in 2021 as he intends, it is sure to spark intense opposition from the far larger number of motorists who will then be affected.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不难想象伦敦也会发生类似的逆转。新的超低排放区（Ulez）很可能成为明年市长选举的一个大问题。如果萨迪克·汗（Sadiq Khan）获胜并按照他的意愿在 2021 年将其扩展到南北环路，那么肯定会引发更多驾车者的强烈反对，届时他们将受到影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s not that measures such as London’s Ulez are useless. Far from it. Local officials are using the levers that are available to them to safeguard residents’ health in the face of a serious threat. The zones do deliver some improvements to air quality, and the science tells us that means real health benefits.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这并不是说伦敦的乌勒兹等措施毫无用处。远非如此。面对严重威胁，当地官员正在利用可用的手段来保护居民的健康。这些区域确实改善了空气质量，科学告诉我们这意味着真正的健康益处。

paragraphs.sourceText: But mayors and councillors can only do so much about a problem that is far bigger than any one city or town. They are acting because national governments — Britain’s and others across Europe — have failed to do so.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但市长和议员们对于这个比任何一个城市或城镇都严重得多的问题只能做这么多。他们之所以采取行动，是因为各国政府——英国和欧洲其他国家的政府——未能这样做。

paragraphs.sourceText: Restrictions that keep highly polluting cars out of certain areas — city centres, “school streets”, even individual roads — are a response to the absence of a larger effort to properly enforce existing regulations and require auto companies to bring their vehicles into compliance. Wales has introduced special low speed limits to minimise pollution. We’re doing everything but insist that manufacturers clean up their cars.
paragraphs.translationZh: 限制高污染汽车进入某些区域——城市中心、“学校街道”，甚至个别道路——是对缺乏更大力度正确执行现有法规并要求汽车公司使其车辆合规的回应。威尔士实行了特殊的低速限制，以尽量减少污染。我们正在尽一切努力，但坚持要求制造商清理他们的汽车。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now that members of Generation Z are graduating college this spring — the most commonly-accepted definition says this generation was born after 1995, give or take a year — the attention has been rising steadily in recent weeks. Gen Zs are about to hit the streets looking for work in a labor market that’s tighter than it’s been in decades. And employers are planning on hiring about 17 percent more new graduates for jobs in the U.S. this year than last, according to a survey conducted by the National Association of Colleges and Employers. Everybody wants to know how the people who will soon inhabit those empty office cubicles will differ from those who came before them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，Z 世代的成员将于今年春天大学毕业——最普遍接受的定义是这一代人出生于 1995 年之后，大约一年左右——最近几周，人们的关注度一直在稳步上升。 Z 世代即将走上街头，在比几十年来更加紧张的劳动力市场中寻找工作。根据全国大学和雇主协会进行的一项调查，今年雇主计划在美国雇用的应届毕业生比去年增加约 17%。每个人都想知道即将入住这些空办公室隔间的人们与之前的人们有何不同。

paragraphs.sourceText: If “entitled” is the most common adjective, fairly or not, applied to millennials (those born between 1981 and 1995), the catchwords for Generation Z are practical and cautious. According to the career counselors and experts who study them, Generation Zs are clear-eyed, economic pragmatists. Despite graduating into the best economy in the past 50 years, Gen Zs know what an economic train wreck looks like. They were impressionable kids during the crash of 2008, when many of their parents lost their jobs or their life savings or both. They aren’t interested in taking any chances. The booming economy seems to have done little to assuage this underlying generational sense of anxious urgency, especially for those who have college debt. College loan balances in the U.S. now stand at a record $1.5 trillion, according to the Federal Reserve.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果“有权利”是最常见的形容词，无论公平与否，适用于千禧一代（1981 年至 1995 年出生的人），那么 Z 世代的口号就是务实和谨慎。根据职业顾问和研究他们的专家的说法，Z 世代是头脑清醒的经济实用主义者。尽管 Z 世代已经进入了过去 50 年来最好的经济体，但他们知道经济列车失事是什么样子。在 2008 年经济危机期间，他们是易受影响的孩子，当时他们的许多父母失去了工作或毕生积蓄，或两者兼而有之。他们没有兴趣冒险。蓬勃发展的经济似乎并没有缓解这一代人潜在的焦虑感，特别是对于那些背负大学债务的人来说。根据美联储的数据，美国的大学贷款余额目前达到创纪录的 1.5 万亿美元。

paragraphs.sourceText: One survey from Accenture found that 88 percent of graduating seniors this year chose their major with a job in mind. In a 2019 survey of University of Georgia students, meanwhile, the career office found the most desirable trait in a future employer was the ability to offer secure employment (followed by professional development and training, and then inspiring purpose). Job security or stability was the second most important career goal (work-life balance was number one), followed by a sense of being dedicated to a cause or to feel good about serving the greater good.
paragraphs.translationZh: 埃森哲的一项调查发现，今年 88% 的应届毕业生在选择专业时就考虑到了工作。与此同时，在 2019 年对佐治亚大学学生的一项调查中，职业办公室发现，未来雇主最理想的特质是提供稳定就业的能力（其次是专业发展和培训，然后是鼓舞人心的目标）。工作保障或稳定是第二重要的职业目标（工作与生活的平衡是第一位的），其次是致力于一项事业的感觉或为更大的利益服务的感觉。

paragraphs.sourceText: That’s a big change from the previous generation. “Millennials wanted more flexibility in their lives,” notes Tanya Michelsen, Associate Director of YouthSight, a UK-based brand manager that conducts regular 60-day surveys of British youth, in findings that might just as well apply to American youth. “Generation Zs are looking for more certainty and stability, because of the rise of the gig economy. They have trouble seeing a financial future and they are quite risk averse.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 这与上一代相比是一个很大的变化。 “千禧一代希望生活更加灵活，”英国品牌管理公司 YouthSight 的副总监 Tanya Michelsen 指出，该公司定期对英国年轻人进行为期 60 天的调查，调查结果也可能适用于美国年轻人。 “由于零工经济的兴起，Z 一代正在寻求更多的确定性和稳定性。他们很难看到财务未来，而且非常厌恶风险。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Five Ways to Win Over Everyone in the Office
paragraphs.translationZh: 赢得办公室每个人的五种方法

paragraphs.sourceText: Is it possible to like everyone in your office? Think about how tough it is to get together 15 people, much less 50, who all get along perfectly. But unlike in friendships, you need coworkers. You work with them every day, and you depend on them just as they depend on you. Here are some ways that you can get the whole office on your side.
paragraphs.translationZh: 有可能喜欢你办公室里的每个人吗？想想看，要让 15 个人（更不用说 50 个人）都相处融洽地聚在一起是多么困难。但与友谊不同的是，你需要同事。您每天与他们一起工作，您依赖他们，就像他们依赖您一样。这里有一些方法可以让整个办公室的人都站在你这边。

paragraphs.sourceText: If you have a bone to pick with someone in your workplace, you may try to stay tight-lipped around them. But you won’t be helping either one of you. A Harvard Business School study found that observers consistently rated those who were frank about themselves more highly, while those who hid lost trustworthiness. The lesson is not that you should make your personal life an open book, but rather, when given the option to offer up details about yourself or painstakingly conceal them, you should just be honest.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果你对工作场所中的某个人有意见，你可能会尝试对他们守口如瓶。但你不会帮助你们任何一个人。哈佛商学院的一项研究发现，观察者一致对那些对自己坦诚的人评价较高，而那些隐藏的人则失去了可信度。我们的教训并不是说你应该让你的个人生活成为一本打开的书，而是当你可以选择提供有关自己的详细信息或刻意隐瞒它们时，你应该诚实。

paragraphs.sourceText: Just as important as being honest about yourself is being receptive to others. We often feel the need to tell others how we feel, whether it’s a concern about a project, a stray thought, or a compliment. Those are all valid, but you need to take time to hear out your coworkers, too. In fact, rushing to get your own ideas out there can cause colleagues to feel you don’t value their opinions. Do your best to engage coworkers in a genuine, back-and-forth conversation, rather than prioritizing your own thoughts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与诚实对待自己一样重要的是接受他人。我们经常觉得有必要告诉别人我们的感受，无论是对项目的担忧、杂念还是赞美。这些都是有效的，但您也需要花时间听取同事的意见。事实上，急于提出自己的想法可能会让同事觉得你不重视他们的意见。尽力与同事进行真诚的、来回的对话，而不是优先考虑自己的想法。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s common to have a “cubicle mate” or special confidant in a work setting. But in addition to those trusted coworkers, you should expand your horizons and find out about all the people around you. Use your lunch and coffee breaks to meet up with colleagues you don’t always see. Find out about their lives and interests beyond the job. It requires minimal effort and goes a long way. This will help to grow your internal network, in addition to being a nice break in the work day.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在工作环境中，有一个“隔间伙伴”或特别知己是很常见的。但除了那些值得信赖的同事之外，你还应该扩大你的视野，了解你周围的所有人。利用午餐和咖啡时间与不常见面的同事见面。了解他们的生活和工作之外的兴趣。它只需要最少的努力，却能起到很大的作用。这除了是工作日的一次愉快的休息之外，还有助于扩大您的内部网络。

paragraphs.sourceText: Positive feedback is important for anyone to hear. And you don’t have to be someone’s boss to tell them they did an exceptional job on a particular project. This will help engender good will in others. But don’t overdo it or be fake about it. One study found that people responded best to comments that shifted from negative to positive, possibly because it suggested they had won somebody over.
paragraphs.translationZh: 积极的反馈对于任何人来说都很重要。而且你不必成为某人的老板才能告诉他们他们在某个特定项目上做得非常出色。这将有助于在他人中产生善意。但不要做得太过分或弄虚作假。一项研究发现，人们对从负面转为正面的评论反应最好，可能是因为这表明他们赢得了某人的支持。

paragraphs.sourceText: This one may be a bit more difficult to pull off, but it can go a long way to achieving results. Remember in dealing with any coworker what they appreciate from an interaction. Watch out for how they verbalize with others. Some people like small talk in a meeting before digging into important matters, while other are more straightforward. Jokes that work on one person won’t necessarily land with another. So, adapt your style accordingly to type. Consider the person that you’re dealing with in advance and what will get you to your desired outcome.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这可能有点难以实现，但它可以对取得成果大有帮助。请记住，在与任何同事打交道时，他们会从互动中欣赏到什么。留意他们如何与他人交谈。有些人喜欢在深入探讨重要问题之前在会议上闲聊，而另一些人则更直截了当。对一个人有效的笑话不一定对另一个人有效。因此，请根据类型调整您的风格。提前考虑一下与你打交道的人以及什么能让你达到你想要的结果。

paragraphs.sourceText: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
paragraphs.translationZh: 将下列文字翻译成中文。将您的翻译写在答题卡上。 （15分）

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s almost impossible to go through life without experiencing some kind of failure. But, the wonderful thing about failure is that it’s entirely up to us to decide how to look at it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一生中几乎不可能不经历某种失败。但是，失败的美妙之处在于，如何看待它完全取决于我们。

paragraphs.sourceText: We can choose to see failure as “the end of the world.” Or, we can look at failure as the incredible learning experience that it often is. Every time we fail at something, we can choose to look for the lesson we’re meant to learn. These lessons are very important; they’re how we grow, and how we keep from making that same mistake again. Failures stop us only if we let them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们可以选择将失败视为“世界末日”。或者，我们可以将失败视为通常令人难以置信的学习经历。每当我们在某件事上失败时，我们都可以选择寻找我们应该吸取的教训。这些教训非常重要；它们是我们成长的方式，也是我们避免再次犯同样错误的方式。只有当我们允许失败时，失败才能阻止我们。

paragraphs.sourceText: Failure can also teach us things about ourselves that we would never have learned otherwise. For instance, failure can help you discover how strong a person you are. Failing at something can help you discover your truest friends, or help you find unexpected motivation to succeed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 失败还可以教会我们一些关于自己的事情，否则我们永远不会学到这些东西。例如，失败可以帮助你发现自己有多坚强。在某件事上失败可以帮助你找到最真诚的朋友，或者帮助你找到意想不到的成功动力。
